139	  disappears on the target side), `type_changed`, `nullable_tightened` —
140	  extended with `nullable_loosened` (only the nullability relaxes) and
141	  `unchanged` (both definitions agree, including both absent); a field that
142	  both changes type and tightens nullability collapses into a single
143	  `type_changed` status. `impacted` lists every field directly or indirectly
144	  downstream of the tracked field for that pair along the lineage mappings,
145	  with the same start-field rule as the pairwise compatibility impact
146	  response (the base version's same-named field and, when it exists, the
147	  target version's); each item is `{"dataset", "version", "field"}`, the set
148	  is deduplicated, never contains a start field itself (cycles terminate),
149	  is sorted by dataset, version and field ascending and is empty when the
150	  field has no downstream. `impacted_datasets` lists the distinct dataset
151	  names appearing in `impacted`, sorted ascending.
152	
153	### Field-level lineage
154	
155	A lineage link maps one field of a target schema version to one field of a
156	schema version in a different (source) dataset.
157	
158	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/lineage` — register a mapping.
159	  Body names both ends:
160	
161	  ```json
162	  {
163	    "target_dataset": "dm_orders",
164	    "target_version": 1,
165	    "target_field": "id",
166	    "source_dataset": "raw_orders",
167	    "source_version": 1,
168	    "source_field": "order_id"
169	  }
170	  ```
171	
172	  Target must match the path. Source and target datasets must differ and every
173	  referenced dataset/version/field must exist (`404` / `422` otherwise).
174	  Submitting the same complete mapping twice returns `409`.
175	- `DELETE /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/lineage` — remove one
176	  registered mapping. Same address and same body shape as registration: the
177	  six locating fields name the complete mapping to delete and the body target
178	  must match the path. Every locating value readable in the request is
179	  resolved first, so an unknown dataset, version or field is a `404` ahead of
180	  every request-shape error; when all six values name existing resources but
181	  the mapping itself was never registered, the delete is likewise a `404`.
182	  An empty or whitespace body, invalid JSON, a non-object payload, missing or
183	  extra fields, wrongly typed values, blank names, any query parameter, a
184	  mapping whose source and target datasets coincide or whose body target
185	  disagrees with the path are all `422`. No rejection changes the lineage
186	  graph, the impact cache or any other metadata. A registered mapping is
187	  deleted atomically and returns `200` with the removed mapping in the
188	  registration response shape; concurrent deletes of the same mapping succeed
189	  exactly once (the loser gets `404` and changes nothing). The deletion is
190	  visible to every lineage read immediately and survives restarts; the cached
191	  impacts of the mapping's source field and of every field that can reach it
192	  are invalidated exactly as on registration, unrelated entries are kept.
193	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/lineage` — return every target
194	  field (including fields without sources) together with its source references.
195	  Results are sorted by target field name, then source dataset name, source
196	  version and source field name.
197	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/lineage/impact?field=<field>` —
198	  return the downstream impact of one source field. The path and the `field`
199	  query parameter together name an existing field; the response is
200	  `{"source": {...}, "impacted": [...]}` where `impacted` lists every field
201	  reachable from the source along lineage mappings (direct and indirect), each
202	  entry being `{"dataset", "version", "field"}`. Results are deduplicated,
203	  never contain the source itself (cycles terminate) and are sorted by dataset,
204	  version and field ascending. Unknown dataset/version/field → `404`; a
205	  missing, blank, invalid or repeated `field` parameter → `422` (a repeated
206	  `field` is judged before the field lookup, so it is always a `422`, never a
207	  field `404`).
208	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/lineage/impact/cache-audit` —
209	  read-only consistency audit of the version's impact cache, appended one
210	  segment after the impact query address. The path dataset and version name
211	  the audit scope; every field of that version is checked against its current
212	  cache record and recomputed fresh from the committed lineage graph using
213	  exactly the impact-query semantics (downstream fields merged and
214	  deduplicated, the start field excluded, cycles terminating). Each entry is
215	  `{"field", "status"}` with `cached` (the stored record equals the
216	  recomputed result), `missing` (no cache record because the field's impact
217	  was never queried — a normal state, not an error) or `mismatch` (the stored
218	  record differs). Entries are sorted by field name ascending and the sort
219	  does not depend on database order. The JSON document is deterministic
220	  (fixed key order, compact whitespace, exactly one trailing newline) with
221	  top-level keys `dataset`, `version`, `entries` and `counts` in that order;
222	  `counts` gives `cached_count`, `missing_count` and `mismatch_count`, each
223	  equal to the number of entries with that status. The audit is computed on
224	  every read and never writes: no cache record is inserted, invalidated or
225	  repaired, so impact queries, impact paths and source paths behave exactly
226	  as before. The endpoint takes no request body and no query parameters; any
227	  body bytes (whitespace-only included) or query parameter → `422`, and an
228	  unknown dataset or version → `404`, with `404` taking precedence over
229	  `422` as in the impact query.
230	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/lineage/impact-paths?field=<field>` —
231	  read-only shortest-path explanation of the same impact, computed fresh on
232	  every read (no caching; nothing is written, and version definitions, lineage
233	  mappings and the impact cache are never touched). The path and the `field`
234	  query parameter together name an existing field. The JSON document is
235	  deterministic (fixed key order, compact whitespace, exactly one trailing
236	  newline) with top-level keys `source`, `impacts`, `direct_count` and
237	  `indirect_count` in that order; `source` is the start field reference
238	  (`{"dataset", "version", "field"}`). Each `impacts` entry has exactly the
239	  location keys `dataset`, `version`, `field`, then `path` and `path_length`;
240	  entries are deduplicated, never contain the source and are sorted by dataset,
241	  version and field ascending. `path` is the shortest node sequence from the
242	  source to the field, including both ends, and each node has the same
243	  `{"dataset", "version", "field"}` shape; `path_length` is the number of
244	  edges on the path (`1` for a direct downstream field, increasing for
245	  indirect ones). Among several shortest paths, the lexicographically smallest
246	  node sequence (compared by dataset, version and field) is chosen; cycles
247	  terminate. `direct_count` counts fields at distance 1 and `indirect_count`
248	  the fields farther away, and a field with no downstream returns an empty
249	  `impacts` array and both counts zero, never an error. The endpoint takes no
250	  request body and no query parameter other than `field` (a missing, blank or
251	  repeated `field` is likewise a `422`); unknown dataset/version/field →
252	  `404`, with `404` taking precedence over every `422` except that a repeated
253	  `field` is judged before the field lookup and is therefore always a `422`.
254	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/lineage/impact/source-paths?field=<field>` —
255	  read-only upstream companion of the lineage impact query, computed fresh on
256	  every read (no caching; nothing is written, and version definitions, lineage
257	  mappings and the impact cache are never touched). The path and the `field`
258	  query parameter together name an existing field; the `field` value is
259	  matched literally (never trimmed), so a whitespace-padded name that matches
260	  no stored field is a `404`. The JSON document is deterministic (fixed key
261	  order, compact whitespace, exactly one trailing newline) with top-level keys
262	  `source`, `origins`, `direct_count`, `indirect_count` and
263	  `source_dataset_count` in that order; `source` is the start field reference
264	  (`{"dataset", "version", "field"}`). Each `origins` entry has exactly the
265	  location keys `dataset`, `version`, `field`, then `path` and `path_length`;
266	  entries are deduplicated, never contain the start field and are sorted by
267	  dataset, version and field ascending. An origin is a field whose mapping
268	  points (directly or transitively) at the start field. `path` is the
269	  shortest node sequence walking from the start field up to the origin,
270	  including both ends, and each node has the same
271	  `{"dataset", "version", "field"}` shape; `path_length` is the number of
272	  edges on the path (`1` for a direct source, increasing for indirect ones).
273	  Among several shortest paths, the lexicographically smallest node sequence
274	  (compared by dataset, version and field) is chosen; cycles terminate.
275	  `direct_count` counts origins at distance 1, `indirect_count` the origins
276	  farther away and `source_dataset_count` the distinct dataset names among
277	  all origins; a field with no sources returns an empty `origins` array and
278	  all counts zero, never an error. The endpoint takes no request body and no
279	  query parameter other than `field` (a missing, blank or repeated `field` is
280	  likewise a `422`); unknown dataset/version/field → `404`, with `404`
281	  taking precedence over every `422` except that a repeated `field` is judged
282	  before the field lookup and is therefore always a `422`.
283	
284	  Impact results are cached persistently (they survive restarts) and every
285	  read reflects the currently committed lineage graph: creating a schema
286	  version invalidates the cache entries related to that dataset, and creating
287	  or deleting a lineage mapping invalidates the cached impacts of the
288	  mapping's source field and of every field that can reach it. Unrelated
289	  cache entries are preserved.
290	
291	### Quality rules
292	
293	Quality rules validate rows against a schema version. Rules are version-scoped
294	and persisted (including their enabled state) across restarts.
295	
296	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/quality-rules` — create a rule.
297	  Body: `{"name": "id required", "kind": "not_null", "params": {...}}`. Returns
298	  `201` with `id`, `name`, `kind`, `params`, `enabled`, `created_at`; `enabled`
299	  defaults to `true`. Rule names must be unique within a version (`409` on
300	  conflict). Referenced dataset/version/field must exist (`404`); other invalid
301	  input returns `422` and nothing is written. Supported kinds:
302	  - `not_null` — params `{"field": "<existing field>"}`.
303	  - `numeric_range` — params `{"field": "<existing field>", "min": <finite
304	    number>, "max": <finite number>}` with `min <= max`.
305	  - `unique` — params `{"fields": ["<existing field>", ...]}`: a non-empty list
306	    of distinct, existing field names.
307	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/quality-rules` — list rules
308	  sorted by `id` ascending.
309	- `PATCH /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/quality-rules/{rule_id}` —
310	  enable or disable a rule. Body: `{"enabled": true}` (boolean only); returns
311	  the updated rule. Unknown rule/dataset/version → `404`.
312	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/quality-rules/evaluate` —
313	  evaluate rows. Body: `{"rows": [{...}, ...]}`. Only enabled rules run.
314	  Returns `{"dataset", "version", "results"}` with results sorted by `rule_id`;
315	  each result has `rule_id`, `name`, `passed` and `violations` (0-based row
316	  indices in ascending order).
317	  - `not_null` fails on missing or `null` values.
318	  - `numeric_range` fails on missing, `null`, non-numeric, boolean or
319	    out-of-range values (boundaries included).
320	  - `unique` compares the tuple of `fields` values per row; a missing field
321	    counts as `null`, and every row taking part in a duplicate group is a
322	    violation.
323	  - With an empty `rows` list every rule passes.
324	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/quality-rules/evaluations` —
325	  list the persisted evaluation history of the version, ordered by `sequence`
326	  (occurrence order). Every successful evaluation appends one immutable
327	  summary (`sequence`, `dataset`, `version`, `row_count`,
328	  `violation_row_count` — the number of distinct submitted rows violating at
329	  least one rule — `results` and `created_at`); rejected or failed
330	  evaluations leave no record, and an empty `rows` submission is recorded
331	  with zero violations. The endpoint takes no request body and no query
332	  parameters (`422`); unknown dataset/version → `404`.
333	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/quality-rules/evaluations/diff`
334	  — read-only diff between the two most recent recorded evaluations
335	  (`from_sequence` → `to_sequence`). `added_violation_rows` /
336	  `removed_violation_rows` are the 0-based row indices that started or
337	  stopped violating any rule, and each entry of `rules` carries the rule's
338	  `before`/`after` side (`violation_count` and `violations`), the per-rule
339	  `added_violations` / `removed_violations` and the numeric
340	  `violation_count_delta` (negative, zero or positive). A rule missing from
341	  one side (disabled or created between the two evaluations) has a `null`
342	  side and `null` row-level diff fields. With fewer than two recorded
343	  evaluations the response is an explicit empty result (null sequences,
344	  empty lists), not an error. Same `404`/`422` rules as the history
345	  endpoint; nothing is written.
346	
347	### Quality anomaly detection
348	
349	Anomaly detection runs over the persisted evaluation history of a schema
350	version. A version carries at most one detection config; scans append
351	immutable anomaly records that persist across restarts.
352	
353	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/quality-rules/anomaly-detection`
354	  — register the version's detection config. The body contains exactly three
355	  integers: `consecutive_worsening_steps` (at least `2`),
356	  `violation_row_limit` and `rule_violation_limit` (both non-negative).
357	  Returns `201` with the config (`id`, `dataset`, `version`, the three
358	  thresholds, `created_at`). A second config for the same version returns
359	  `409`; unknown dataset/version → `404`; missing, extra, non-integer or
360	  out-of-range fields → `422` and nothing is written.
361	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/quality-rules/anomaly-detection`
362	  — return the registered config (`404` when none exists). The endpoint takes
363	  no request body and no query parameters (`422`).
364	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/quality-rules/anomaly-detection/scan`
365	  — run one detection pass over the persisted evaluation history and return
366	  the anomaly records this scan newly added (ordered by `id`); they are
367	  persisted in the same transaction. Scanning without a registered config
368	  returns `409`; an empty history is a successful scan that writes nothing.
369	  The endpoint takes no request body and no query parameters (`422`). Each
370	  record has `id`, `kind`, `sequence` (the history sequence it points to),
371	  `rule_id`, `violation_count` and `created_at`; `kind` is one of:
372	  - `row_limit` — the evaluation's `violation_row_count` exceeds
373	    `violation_row_limit` (`rule_id` is `null`).
374	  - `rule_limit` — one rule's violation count in the evaluation exceeds
375	    `rule_violation_limit`; `rule_id` carries the rule's id.
376	  - `trend` — the violation row counts of adjacent evaluations strictly
377	    increase and the consecutive increase count at the tail of the history
378	    reaches `consecutive_worsening_steps`; the record points to the final
379	    evaluation of the increasing sequence (`rule_id` is `null`). A shorter
380	    run or any decline produces no trend record.
381	
382	  A record with the same kind, history sequence and rule id is never
383	  duplicated: repeated scans only persist and return newly appearing
384	  anomalies, and concurrent scans store each anomaly exactly once with
385	  contiguous ids.
386	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/quality-rules/anomaly-detection/anomalies`
387	  — list every anomaly record of the version sorted by `id` ascending (empty
388	  when there are none, never an error). Same `404`/`422` rules as the scan
389	  endpoint; nothing is written.
390	
391	### Quality gate
392	
393	The quality gate is the release-readiness verdict of a schema version. It is
394	computed fresh from the persisted records on every read — nothing is cached,
395	re-run or written, and the rule definitions are never consulted (violations
396	recorded for rules since disabled still count).
397	
398	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/quality-rules/gate` — return the
399	  verdict as a deterministic JSON document (fixed key order, compact
400	  whitespace, exactly one trailing newline):
401	  `{"dataset", "version", "verdict", "reasons", "counts"}`.
402	  - `verdict` is one of:
403	    - `pass` — the latest recorded evaluation passed every rule and no
404	      anomaly record exists; a zero-violation evaluation left by an empty
405	      `rows` submission is a valid basis.
406	    - `undetermined` — no evaluation was ever recorded; `reasons` is empty
407	      and the read succeeds (never an error).
408	    - `fail` — the latest recorded evaluation still has violating rows, or
409	      the version carries any anomaly record.
410	  - `reasons` lists every factor that lowers the verdict, sorted by `kind`,
411	    `sequence` and `rule_id` (null ids first), all ascending. Each reason has
412	    `kind`, `sequence`, `rule_id` and `violation_count` (a missing rule id is
413	    `null`, never omitted). Every rule with violations in the latest
414	    evaluation contributes one `violation` reason with its violation row
415	    count; every persisted anomaly record contributes one reason of its own
416	    kind (`row_limit`, `rule_limit` or `trend`). A rule that appears in both
417	    yields two reasons — they are never merged or deduplicated.
418	  - `counts` reports how many persisted records the verdict examined:
419	    `evaluations`, `anomalies` and `reasons` (the length of the reason list).
420	  - The endpoint takes no request body and no query parameters: any body
421	    bytes — including whitespace-only ones — or any query parameter are a
422	    `422`, checked after the path dataset/version resolves (`404` first).
423	    Nothing is written on any rejection.
424	
425	### Privacy policies
426	
427	Privacy policies attach a sensitivity classification and masking strategy to a
428	single field of a schema version, enabling role-based de-identification of row
429	data. Policies (including their enabled state) are persisted across restarts.
430	
431	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/privacy-policies` — register a
432	  policy. Body:
433	  `{"field": "email", "classification": "PII", "masking": "partial", "allowed_roles": ["analyst"]}`.
434	  `field` must name an existing field of the version; `classification` is a
435	  non-empty string; `masking` is `redact` or `partial`; `allowed_roles` is an
436	  array of distinct, non-empty role names and may be empty. Returns `201` with
437	  the submitted fields plus `id`, `enabled` (defaults to `true`) and
438	  `created_at`. Registering two policies for the same field within one version
439	  returns `409`. Unknown dataset/version/field → `404`; other invalid input →
440	  `422` and nothing is written.
441	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/privacy-policies` — list policies
442	  sorted by `id` ascending.
443	- `PATCH /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/privacy-policies/{policy_id}` —
444	  enable or disable a policy. Body: `{"enabled": true}` (boolean only); returns
445	  the updated policy. Unknown policy/dataset/version → `404`.
446	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/privacy-policies/view` — return a
447	  role-scoped, order-preserving copy of submitted rows. Body:
448	  `{"role": "guest", "rows": [{...}, ...]}` with a non-empty `role` and a list
449	  of row objects. Response: `{"dataset", "version", "rows"}`. Only enabled
450	  policies whose field appears in a row mask the value when `role` is not in
451	  `allowed_roles`:
452	  - `redact` replaces every non-`null` value with `"***"`.
453	  - `partial` keeps the first character and last two characters of strings
454	    longer than 4 characters (e.g. `"alice@example.com"` → `"aom"`); every other
455	    non-`null` value (short strings, numbers, booleans, …) is replaced with
456	    `"***"`.
457	  - `null` values and fields without a policy are returned unchanged; rows
458	    missing a covered field are left without it.
459	
460	  Every successful view also appends one audit record per value it actually
461	  masked (the same field masked in several rows yields one record per masked
462	  value; a role in `allowed_roles`, a `null` value, an uncovered field or a
463	  disabled policy never hits); the records are persisted per version and are
464	  append-only.
465	
466	  Every successful view additionally appends exactly one access record,
467	  whether or not it masked any value (an empty `rows` submission is recorded
468	  too). Rejected or failed views leave neither kind of record.
469	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/privacy-policies/view/access-records`
470	  — list every access record of the version, ordered by `sequence` ascending
471	  (empty when there are none, never an error). Each record has `sequence`,
472	  `role`, `row_count` (the number of submitted rows), `masked_count` (the
473	  number of masking-hit records the same view wrote, so the two logs
474	  cross-check) and `created_at`. The endpoint takes no request body and no
475	  query parameters (`422`); unknown dataset/version → `404`. Nothing is
476	  written.
477	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/privacy-policies/view/audit-records`
478	  — list every masking-hit record of the version, ordered by `sequence`
479	  ascending (empty when there are none, never an error). Each record has
480	  `sequence`, `field`, `policy_id`, `role`, `masking` and `created_at`. The
481	  endpoint takes no request body and no query parameters (`422`); unknown
482	  dataset/version → `404`. Nothing is written.
483	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/privacy-policies/view/audit-records/search`
484	  — read-only filtered retrieval of the same masking-hit records. The
485	  response is the same record collection as the full list (each record has
486	  `sequence`, `field`, `policy_id`, `role`, `masking` and `created_at`),
487	  sorted by `sequence` ascending; a filter that matches nothing returns an
488	  empty array, never an error. All filters are optional query parameters and
489	  combine with AND:
490	  - `role` — exact match against the requesting role recorded on the hit,
491	    case-insensitive (no substring or other fuzzy matching).
492	  - `field` — exact match against the hit field name, case-insensitive.
493	  - `start` / `end` — closed write-time interval: a record matches when its
494	    `created_at` is between the bounds inclusive. Each bound is a
495	    timezone-bearing ISO-8601 date-time (offset or `Z`); either bound may be
496	    given alone. `start` later than `end` → `422`.
497	
498	  The endpoint takes no request body; an unparseable or timezone-less
499	  `start`/`end`, or any query parameter other than `role`, `field`, `start`
500	  and `end`, → `422`. Unknown dataset/version → `404`, with the same
501	  404-before-422 precedence as the record list. It is strictly read-only:
502	  no record is written, modified or deleted and the summary/diff responses
503	  are unaffected.
504	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/privacy-policies/view/audit-records/summary`
505	  — read-only compliance summary computed fresh from the persisted records on
506	  every read (no caching, nothing is written or deleted). Response:
507	  `{"dataset", "version", "groups"}`; `groups` is an empty array when the
508	  version has no records. Each group merges records with the same `field`,
509	  `policy_id`, `role` and `masking` (different roles or masking modes stay
510	  separate) and lists `field`, `policy_id`, `role`, `masking`, `hit_count`
511	  (one record counts as one hit), `first_hit_at` and `last_hit_at` (the
512	  earliest and latest record `created_at` in the group). Groups sort by
513	  `field`, then `policy_id`, `role` and `masking`, all ascending. The
514	  endpoint takes no request body and no query parameters (`422`); unknown
515	  dataset/version → `404`, with the same 404-before-422 precedence as the
516	  record list.
517	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/privacy-policies/view/audit-records/trend`
518	  — read-only hit trend aggregated by privacy policy, computed fresh from the
519	  persisted records on every read (no caching, nothing is written or deleted).
520	  Hits of the same policy merge across roles (a disabled policy's historical
521	  hits still count). Response: `{"dataset", "version", "policies", "totals"}`;
522	  `policies` is an empty array when the version has no records. Each policy
523	  row carries `policy_id`, `field`, `classification`, `masking`, `total_hits`
524	  and `days`; policies sort by `policy_id` ascending. `days` lists only UTC
525	  calendar days with hits (a write time with a non-zero offset buckets by its
526	  UTC day), sorted ascending with no zero-filled gaps; each entry has `day`
527	  (`YYYY-MM-DD`), `hit_count` (one record counts once), `hit_count_delta`
528	  (difference from the previous listed day, `null` on the first) and `trend`
529	  (`up`/`down`/`flat`, or `none` on the first day). `totals` gives
530	  `total_hits` (the sum of the row totals), `policy_count` (policies with
531	  hits) and `day_count` (distinct hit days over the whole version, the
532	  per-policy day union). The endpoint takes no request body and no query
533	  parameters (`422`); unknown dataset/version → `404`, with the same
534	  404-before-422 precedence as the record list.
535	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/privacy-policies/view/audit-records/cleanup-requests`
536	  — open a two-stage retention cleanup request for the version's masking-hit
537	  records. Body contains exactly `reason` and `before`:
538	  `{"reason": "legal hold expired", "before": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"}`.
539	  `reason` must be a string that is non-empty after trimming whitespace;
540	  `before` must be an ISO-8601 date-time carrying a timezone (offset or `Z`),
541	  and a record belongs to the target set only when its hit write time is
542	  strictly earlier than that instant. Creating a request only returns a
543	  preview — no hit record is deleted or modified, and the record list,
544	  search, summary, diff, reconcile and trend responses stay unchanged.
545	  Returns `201` with `id`, `reason` (trimmed), `before` (echoed as
546	  submitted), `status` (`pending`), `created_at` and a `preview` block:
547	  `hit_count` (the number of records that would be cleaned up),
548	  `first_hit_at` / `last_hit_at` (the earliest and latest hit times in the
549	  target set, `null` when the set is empty) and `fields` (the distinct field
550	  names involved, sorted ascending; `[]` when empty). The target set is
551	  fixed at creation time: masking-hit records written afterwards never enter
552	  the request even when they precede the cutoff by clock time. At most one
553	  pending request may exist per version; creating another while one is open
554	  returns `409` and writes nothing (confirmed requests never block a new
555	  one). Unknown dataset/version → `404`; missing/non-string/blank `reason`,
556	  missing/unparseable/timezone-less `before`, an extra body field, a
557	  non-JSON/non-object body or any query parameter → `422` and nothing is
558	  written, with 404 taking precedence.
559	- `GET .../privacy-policies/view/audit-records/cleanup-requests` — list the
560	  version's cleanup requests sorted by request `id` ascending (empty when
561	  there are none). Confirmed requests stay listed and requests survive
562	  process restarts. The endpoint takes no request body and no query
563	  parameters (`422`); unknown dataset/version → `404`.
564	- `POST .../privacy-policies/view/audit-records/cleanup-requests/{request_id}/confirm`
565	  — confirm a request with an empty request body and no query parameters.
566	  Confirmation atomically deletes exactly the target set frozen at creation
567	  and sets `status` to `confirmed`; the response is the request plus
568	  `confirmed_at` and `deleted_count` (the number of records actually
569	  deleted, possibly zero). Confirming an already-confirmed request returns
570	  `409` and never changes data again; concurrent confirmations have exactly
571	  one winner (the others get `409`) and can never leave the records half
572	  deleted. After a cleanup the surviving hit records keep their original
573	  `sequence` numbers and later hits continue the existing increasing run
574	  without reusing cleaned numbers; the record list and search return only
575	  surviving records, and summary, trend, diff and reconcile recompute from
576	  them. Access records are not cleaned up and the processing-task audit
577	  chain remains immutable. A request body or query parameter on the confirm
578	  endpoint → `422`; unknown dataset/version/request → `404` (precedence
579	  matches the hit-record reads), and confirming a confirmed request →
580	  `409`.
581	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/privacy-compliance-export` — read-only
582	  cross-version export of the dataset's whole privacy compliance state,
583	  computed fresh on every read (no caching; nothing is written, modified or
584	  deleted, and no hit record, access record or cleanup request is touched).
585	  The path carries only the dataset name; the request takes no body and no
586	  query parameters (`422`); an unknown dataset → `404`, with the same
587	  404-before-422 precedence as the hit-record reads. A dataset without
588	  schema versions returns `200` with an empty `versions` array and all-zero
589	  totals, never an error. The JSON document is deterministic (fixed key
590	  order, compact whitespace, exactly one trailing newline):
591	
592	  ```json
593	  {"dataset":"orders","versions":[{"version":1,"policies":[...],"hit_count":0,"masked_count":1,"view_count":2,"cleanup_requests":[...]}],"totals":{...}}
594	  ```
595	
596	  The top-level keys are exactly `dataset`, `versions`, `totals` in that
597	  order. `versions` is ordered by version number ascending and each entry
598	  has exactly `version`, `policies`, `hit_count`, `masked_count`,
599	  `view_count`, `cleanup_requests` in that order. `policies` lists the
600	  version's registered policies ordered by policy id; each policy has `id`,
601	  `field`, `classification`, `masking`, `allowed_roles` and `enabled`.
602	  `cleanup_requests` lists the version's cleanup requests ordered by request
603	  id (both pending and confirmed are retained); each has `id`, `reason`,
604	  `status` and `created_at`. `hit_count` is the number of masking-hit
605	  records currently stored for the version, `masked_count` is the sum of the
606	  access records' masked-value counts and `view_count` is the number of
607	  access records; all three reflect the records surviving a confirmed
608	  cleanup. `totals` has exactly `policy_count`, `hit_count`, `masked_count`,
609	  `view_count` and `cleanup_request_count`, each the sum of the per-version
610	  values over the whole dataset.
611	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/privacy-policy-coverage` — read-only cross-version
612	  check of the dataset's privacy policy coverage, computed fresh on every
613	  read (no caching; nothing is written, modified or deleted, and no policy
614	  or identification record is touched). The path carries only the dataset
615	  name; the request takes no body and no query parameters (`422`); an
616	  unknown dataset → `404`, with the same 404-before-422 precedence as the
617	  compliance export. A dataset without schema versions returns `200` with an
618	  empty `versions` array and all-zero totals, never an error. The JSON
619	  document is deterministic (fixed key order, compact whitespace, exactly
620	  one trailing newline):
621	
622	  ```json
623	  {"dataset":"orders","versions":[{"version":1,"fields":[...],"candidates":[...]}],"totals":{...}}
624	  ```
625	
626	  The top-level keys are exactly `dataset`, `versions`, `totals` in that
627	  order. `versions` is ordered by version number ascending and each entry
628	  has exactly `version`, `fields`, `candidates` in that order. `fields`
629	  lists every field of the version ordered by field name; each entry has
630	  `field`, `coverage`, `classification`, `masking` and `enabled`, where
631	  `coverage` is `enabled` (an enabled policy is registered), `disabled` (a
632	  policy is registered but disabled) or `unregistered` (no policy), and the
633	  last three keys report the registered policy's classification, masking and
634	  enabled state (all `null` when no policy is registered). `candidates`
635	  lists the advisory suggestions for fields that were identified with at
636	  least one name or sample hit but carry no privacy policy yet, ordered by
637	  identification record id ascending; each candidate has exactly `field`,
638	  `classification` and `masking`, and an identified field whose name and
639	  samples both missed does not appear. The candidates are a compliance
640	  self-check reference only: they never register a policy and never rewrite
641	  an identification record. `totals` has exactly `version_count`,
642	  `field_count`, `enabled_count`, `disabled_count`, `unregistered_count`
643	  and `candidate_count`, each the sum of the per-version values over the
644	  whole dataset.
645	
646	### Sensitive-field identification
647	
648	Sensitive-field identification produces candidate annotations for the fields of
649	a schema version. It complements the manual privacy policies but never creates
650	or modifies one: an identification is advisory only. Records (including their
651	stable ids) persist across restarts.
652	
653	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/sensitive-identifications` —
654	  identify one field. The body contains exactly `field` and `samples`:
655	  `{"field": "contact_email", "samples": ["alice@example.com"]}`. `field` must
656	  name an existing field of the version; its name and type are taken from the
657	  version definition. `samples` is an array of JSON scalars (strings, numbers,
658	  booleans or `null`) and may be empty; objects or arrays reject the whole
659	  request. The samples are never stored or echoed back. Returns the record;
660	  the first submission for a field returns `201`, re-running the same field
661	  refreshes the record in place (the id is unchanged) and returns `200`.
662	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/sensitive-identifications` —
663	  return every identification record of the version sorted by id ascending
664	  (empty when there are none). The endpoint takes no request body and no query
665	  parameters (`422`); unknown dataset/version → `404`.
666	
667	  Each record has `id`, `field`, `field_type`, `evidence`, `confidence`,
668	  `source` and `created_at`. `source` references the identified field as
669	  `{"dataset", "version", "field"}`. `evidence` is the ordered, de-duplicated
670	  list of hit kinds, name hits before sample hits:
671	
672	  - **Name hits** — the field name contains a sensitive word case-insensitively
673	    as a substring. The words are `email`, `phone`, `id_card`, `password`,
674	    `token` and `birth`, emitting `name:<word>` in that order.
675	  - **Sample hits** — only string sample values are inspected (numbers,
676	    booleans and `null` never hit), and only when the field's declared type is
677	    `string`; a field declared with any other type is matched by name alone,
678	    even when a sample looks like an email. `sample:email` requires exactly
679	    one `@` with non-empty text on both sides and a dot in the domain;
680	    `sample:phone` requires an 11-digit string starting with `1`. Either format
681	    matching is sufficient.
682	
683	  `confidence` is `high` when both the name and the samples hit, `medium` for
684	  samples only, `low` for the name only and `none` when neither side hits
685	  (`evidence` is then an empty list but the record is still generated).
686	
687	  One record is kept per field: a re-run overwrites the evidence and confidence
688	  in place with a stable id. Unknown dataset/version → `404`; a field that does
689	  not exist in the version → `404`; missing or extra body fields, a
690	  non-string or blank field name, a `samples` value that is not an array of
691	  scalars (objects and arrays included), an empty body, malformed JSON or any
692	  query parameter → `422` and nothing is written.
693	
694	#### Masking strategy suggestions
695	
696	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/sensitive-identifications/masking-suggestions`
697	  — read-only advisory masking-strategy candidates derived from the version's
698	  identification records. The endpoint takes no request body and no query
699	  parameters (`422` if either is present, with nothing written); unknown
700	  dataset/version → `404`. A version without identification records returns an
701	  empty list rather than an error.
702	
703	  Each candidate has exactly `field`, `classification`, `masking` and
704	  `allowed_roles`. Only records whose name or samples hit produce a candidate;
705	  a record with empty evidence is omitted. Candidates follow the identification
706	  records' `id` ascending and are recomputed on every read, so refreshing an
707	  identification changes the suggestion on the next request. The endpoint
708	  writes nothing, never registers a privacy policy and leaves the
709	  identification records' fields, ordering and refresh semantics untouched;
710	  the privacy view continues to mask according to registered policies only.
711	
712	  - `classification` is `PII` for email, phone, id-card and birthday hits, and
713	    `CREDENTIAL` for password and token hits. A field hitting both is `PII`.
714	  - `masking` reuses the privacy-view vocabulary: `partial` for `PII`
715	    candidates and `redact` for `CREDENTIAL` candidates (a both-kinds field
716	    takes `partial`); no new masking format is introduced.
717	  - `allowed_roles` is always an empty list: the suggested masking applies to
718	    every role, granting none an unmasked view.
719	
720	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/sensitive-identifications/masking-suggestions/register`
721	  — turn the current advisory candidates into registered privacy policies. The
722	  body contains only `{"fields": ["<field>", ...]}`: a non-empty array of
723	  distinct field names, each non-empty after trimming and naming an existing
724	  field of the version that currently has a masking suggestion candidate.
725	  Returns `201` with one privacy policy record per requested field, in the
726	  request's field-name order; each record has the same fields as the manual
727	  policy creation response (`id`, `field`, `classification`, `masking`,
728	  `allowed_roles`, `enabled`, `created_at`), is enabled by default and gets a
729	  service-generated id and timestamp. Each policy copies its candidate's
730	  `classification` and `masking` verbatim with the candidate's empty
731	  `allowed_roles`, so after registration every role sees those fields masked;
732	  the next privacy view read masks according to the new policies. The whole
733	  batch is validated before anything is written, so any rejection writes no
734	  policy and no timestamp. Unknown dataset/version, or a named field that does
735	  not exist in the version → `404`; a field without an available candidate
736	  (never identified, or whose identification record currently yields no
737	  candidate) or one that already has a privacy policy → `409`; two concurrent
738	  registrations of the same field leave exactly one winner. Missing or extra
739	  body fields, an empty `fields` array, duplicate, non-string or blank names,
740	  an empty body, a whitespace-only body, malformed JSON or any query parameter
741	  → `422` and nothing is written. Registration only reads the identification
742	  records and field definitions; it never writes or auto-refreshes an
743	  identification, and the read-only suggestions endpoint stays unchanged.
744	
745	### Row snapshots
746	
747	A row snapshot persistently records the rows of a schema version at one point in
748	time. Snapshots (including their rows) survive restarts.
749	
750	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/snapshots` — persist a snapshot.
751	  Body: `{"rows": [{...}, ...]}` where `rows` must be an array of JSON objects
752	  (it may be empty). The JSON values and the order of rows/object keys are deep
753	  copied verbatim. Returns `201` with `id`, `dataset`, `version`,
754	  `created_at` and `row_count` (no rows). Unknown dataset/version → `404`;
755	  malformed or non-object rows → `422` and nothing is written.
756	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/snapshots` — list snapshot
757	  metadata sorted by `id` ascending (no `rows`).
758	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/snapshots/{snapshot_id}` — return
759	  the metadata together with the saved `rows`. Unknown dataset/version/snapshot
760	  → `404`.
761	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/snapshots/at?timestamp=<ISO-8601>` —
762	  return the most recent snapshot whose `created_at` is not later than
763	  `timestamp`, including its rows. The timestamp must be a timezone-aware
764	  ISO-8601 date-time (an offset or trailing `Z`): missing, invalid or
765	  timezone-less values return `422`; unknown dataset/version → `404`; when no
766	  snapshot exists at or before the timestamp the response is `404`.
767	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/snapshots/{snapshot_id}/diff/{other_snapshot_id}` —
768	  compare two snapshots as JSON-object multisets. Object key order does not
769	  affect equality, while array order and JSON value types do (e.g. `1`, `1.0`,
770	  `"1"` and `true` are all distinct), and duplicate rows are counted. Both
771	  snapshots must belong to the dataset and version named in the path, otherwise
772	  `422`; unknown dataset/version/snapshot → `404`. The response is
773	  `{"from_snapshot_id", "to_snapshot_id", "added", "removed"}`; `added` lists
774	  rows present more often (or only) in the `to` snapshot and `removed` the
775	  converse, each entry being `{"row": {...}, "count": <int>}` sorted by the
776	  canonical (key-sorted) JSON text of `row`.
777	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/snapshots/{snapshot_id}/quality-rules/evaluate`
778	  — evaluate the version's enabled quality rules over the snapshot's persisted
779	  rows. The endpoint takes no request body and no query parameters (`422`);
780	  unknown dataset/version/snapshot → `404` (checked first), and a snapshot
781	  owned by another version → `422`. The response and the rule semantics are
782	  exactly those of the row-submission evaluation (`{"dataset", "version",
783	  "results"}`), the snapshot and its rows are never modified, and every
784	  successful evaluation appends the same immutable history summary (with
785	  `row_count` set to the snapshot's actual row count) that also feeds the
786	  evaluation diff and anomaly detection. An empty snapshot is recorded with
787	  zero violations.
788	
789	### Retention policies and lineage-aware snapshot deletion
790	
791	A schema version can carry a single retention policy; snapshot deletion is a
792	two-stage request/confirm flow that refuses to remove snapshots still feeding
793	downstream fields. Policies and requests are persisted across restarts.
794	
795	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/retention-policies` — create the
796	  version's one retention policy. Body: `{"retention_days": 30}` with a
797	  non-negative integer. Returns `201` with `id`, `dataset`, `version`,
798	  `retention_days`, `created_at`. A second policy for the same version returns
799	  `409`; unknown dataset/version → `404`; other invalid input → `422`.
800	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/snapshots/{snapshot_id}/deletion-requests` —
801	  request deletion. Body contains only a non-empty `reason`. The snapshot and
802	  the version's retention policy must exist. Returns `201` with `id`,
803	  `snapshot_id`, `policy_id`, `reason`, `status`, `impacted`, `created_at`.
804	  `impacted` lists every field directly or indirectly reachable downstream of
805	  any field of the snapshot's version along lineage mappings; entries are
806	  deduplicated and sorted by dataset, version and field ascending. The request
807	  is `blocked` when any downstream field exists and `pending` otherwise. A
808	  second `pending`/`blocked` request for the same snapshot returns `409`.
809	- `GET .../snapshots/{snapshot_id}/deletion-requests` — list the snapshot's
810	  deletion requests sorted by `id` ascending. The collection remains
811	  addressable after a confirmed request has deleted its snapshot.
812	- `POST .../snapshots/{snapshot_id}/deletion-requests/{request_id}/confirm` —
813	  confirm a request (no body). Confirmation succeeds only while the request is
814	  `pending` and the snapshot is at least `retention_days` old; otherwise `409`
815	  and nothing is deleted. On success the snapshot is deleted atomically with
816	  the status change to `confirmed`, and the response adds `confirmed_at`. Once
817	  deleted, the snapshot no longer appears in snapshot read, list, `at` or diff
818	  responses.
819	
820	  Unknown dataset/version/snapshot/policy/request → `404`; other invalid input
821	  → `422` and nothing is written.
822	
823	### Processing tasks
824	
825	A processing task is a named unit of work attached to a schema version; each
826	run records one attempt. Tasks and runs are persisted across restarts.
827	
828	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/processing-tasks` — create a
829	  task. Body: `{"name": "extract", "depends_on": [1], "max_attempts": 3}`.
830	  `name` must be non-empty and unique within the version (`409` on conflict);
831	  `depends_on` is an array of distinct task ids from the same version (default
832	  `[]`, unknown ids → `404`); `max_attempts` is a positive integer (default
833	  `1`). Returns `201` with `id`, `dataset`, `version`, `name`, `depends_on`,
834	  `max_attempts`, `status` (`pending`), `attempt_count` (`0`) and
835	  `created_at`. Other invalid input → `422` and nothing is written.
836	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/processing-tasks` — list tasks
837	  sorted by `id` ascending.
838	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/processing-tasks/{task_id}` —
839	  return the task together with its `runs`, sorted by `attempt` ascending.
840	  Each run has `id`, `task_id`, `attempt`, `status`, `started_at`,
841	  `finished_at` and `error`. Unknown dataset/version/task → `404`.
842	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/processing-tasks/{task_id}/runs` —
843	  start a new run. Only allowed while the task is `pending` or `failed`, has
844	  attempts left (`attempt_count < max_attempts`) and every task in
845	  `depends_on` has status `succeeded`; otherwise `409` and nothing is written.
846	  Returns `201` with the new `running` run and increments the task's
847	  `attempt_count` (the task becomes `running`).
848	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/processing-tasks/dispatch` —
849	  worker batch claim. The body is optional and contains only an optional
850	  `limit`: omit the body (or send `{}`) to claim one task, or send
851	  `{"limit": <positive integer>}`. Within a single transaction, up to `limit`
852	  startable tasks are selected by task id ascending; a task is startable when
853	  it is `pending`, or `failed` with attempts left, and every direct dependency
854	  is `succeeded` at selection time. Each selected task gets a new `running`
855	  run for its next attempt, `attempt_count` is incremented and the task becomes
856	  `running`. `running`, `succeeded`, attempt-exhausted and dependency-blocked
857	  tasks are skipped; a task started earlier in the same request is only
858	  `running`, so its dependents are not selectable until a later request.
859	  Returns `201` with `{"dataset", "version", "runs"}`; `runs` is sorted by
860	  task id ascending and each run has the same fields as the single-task start
861	  endpoint. When no task is startable the response is still `201` with an
862	  empty `runs` list. Concurrent dispatches (and dispatches interleaved with
863	  single-task starts) never create a duplicate attempt or two running runs for
864	  the same task, and a single response never exceeds `limit`. Unknown
865	  dataset/version → `404`; extra body fields, a non-integer (including
866	  boolean) or non-positive `limit` → `422` and nothing is written.
867	- `PATCH /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/processing-tasks/{task_id}/runs/{run_id}` —
868	  finish the currently running run. Body: `{"status": "succeeded"}` or
869	  `{"status": "failed", "error": "<non-empty message>"}`. Writes `finished_at`
870	  and moves the task to the same status; a `failed` task with attempts left
871	  can be started again. Finishing an already finished run → `409`; a run that
872	  does not belong to the task/version in the path → `422`; unknown
873	  dataset/version/task/run → `404`; other invalid input → `422` and nothing
874	  is written.
875	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/processing-tasks/batch-complete` —
876	  finish several currently running runs in one transaction. Body contains only
877	  a non-empty `runs` array; each item names a task of the path version and one
878	  of its runs: `{"task_id": <int>, "run_id": <int>, "status": "succeeded"}` or
879	  the same with `"status": "failed"` and an `error` that is non-empty after
880	  trimming whitespace (`succeeded` items carry no `error`). The same task must
881	  not appear twice. The whole batch is validated before any write and either
882	  every item completes or none do; on success the response is
883	  `{"dataset", "version", "runs"}` with the completed runs sorted by task id
884	  ascending, each carrying the same fields as the single-run finish response.
885	  Every run gets a `finished_at` timestamp and its task moves atomically to
886	  the same status; `failed` tasks keep their consumed attempts and stay
887	  retryable while attempts remain. Tasks whose dependencies succeed in the
888	  same batch are not started or skipped within that batch (the dependencies
889	  are `running` at selection time, as with dispatch) and become startable
890	  immediately afterwards, each at its next continuous attempt. Empty/missing
891	  `runs`, extra fields, non-integer (including boolean) ids, an unknown status
892	  or a missing/blank/non-string `error` → `422`; an empty body or malformed
893	  JSON → `422`; any query parameter → `422`. Unknown dataset/version → `404`;
894	  a batch task that does not exist or belongs to another dataset/version →
895	  `404`; an unknown run → `404` (a run belonging to another dataset/version is
896	  treated as out of scope); a run that belongs to another task of the same
897	  version → `422`. An already finished run, a duplicate task in the batch or a
898	  task that is not currently `running` (not currently completable) → `409`,
899	  and the entire batch is rolled back: statuses, timestamps and counters are
900	  unchanged. Concurrent batch completion is single-winner against the
901	  single-run finish/cancel endpoints, run starts and batch dispatch: exactly
902	  one racing operation commits and the others receive `409`, never leaving a
903	  `running` run with a half-written `finished_at` or rolling `attempt_count`
904	  back. Audit records appended afterwards record the run's terminal status,
905	  and the schedule, audit report and post-restart reads present the batch
906	  results through the existing fields and ordering.
907	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/processing-tasks/{task_id}/runs/{run_id}/cancel` —
908	  cancel the currently running run. The body contains only a non-empty
909	  `reason` string; leading and trailing whitespace is trimmed and the result
910	  is stored as the run's `error`. Returns the updated run with `finished_at`
911	  written and `status` `failed`; the task is atomically moved to `failed` in
912	  the same transaction while `attempt_count` is not rolled back, so a
913	  cancelled task follows the existing start rules: it can run again when its
914	  dependencies have succeeded and attempts remain, and the next run keeps the
915	  continuous attempt sequence. Only a `running` run can be cancelled;
916	  cancelling an already `succeeded`/`failed` run returns `409` and changes no
917	  field. A run that does not belong to the task/version in the path → `422`;
918	  unknown dataset/version/task/run → `404`; a missing reason, an extra body
919	  field, a non-string reason or one that is blank after trimming, an empty
920	  body, malformed JSON or any query parameter → `422` and nothing is
921	  written. Cancellation is single-winner against finishing, single-task
922	  starts and batch dispatch: exactly one racing operation performs the state
923	  transition and the others receive `409`, so no run is left `running` with a
924	  half-written `finished_at`.
925	- `PUT /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/processing-tasks/{task_id}/dependencies` —
926	  atomically replace the task's dependency list. Body contains only
927	  `{"depends_on": [<task id>, ...]}` (the array may be empty); the ids must
928	  reference existing tasks of the same version without duplicates and must not
929	  include the target task itself. The replacement is rejected when the target
930	  task is not `pending` or when it would introduce a cycle in the dependency
931	  graph; on success the updated task is returned. Unknown
932	  dataset/version/task/dependency → `404`; a self dependency, a cycle or a
933	  non-`pending` target → `409`; any other invalid body → `422` and nothing is
934	  written. The existing run-start rule uses the updated dependencies.
935	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/processing-tasks/schedule` —
936	  return `{"dataset", "version", "tasks"}` with tasks sorted by `id` ascending.
937	  Each task carries every processing-task field plus `schedule_state` and
938	  `blocking_task_ids`. `schedule_state` is `running` or `succeeded` for tasks
939	  in those states; a `failed` task is `retryable` while attempts remain and
940	  `exhausted` once they are used up; a `pending` task is `ready` when all of
941	  its direct dependencies have succeeded, `upstream_failed` when any
942	  dependency chain contains an `exhausted` or `upstream_failed` task, and
943	  `blocked` otherwise. `blocking_task_ids` lists the direct dependencies that
944	  have not succeeded, sorted ascending; it is empty for non-pending tasks.
945	  States are recomputed on every read (including after a successful retry)
946	  and both the dependency graph and the schedule survive restarts.
947	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/processing-tasks/audit-report` —
948	  read-only audit report for the whole version; the endpoint takes no request
949	  body and no query parameters (both are rejected with `422`; unknown
950	  dataset/version → `404`). Returns
951	  `{"dataset", "version", "summary", "tasks"}`. `summary` contains
952	  `task_count`, `run_count`, `pending_tasks`, `running_tasks`,
953	  `succeeded_tasks`, `failed_tasks`, `exhausted_tasks` and
954	  `invalid_audit_runs`; status counters count tasks by their stored status,
955	  `exhausted_tasks` counts `failed` tasks that have used up
956	  `max_attempts`, and `invalid_audit_runs` counts runs whose audit chain fails
957	  re-verification. `tasks` is sorted by task `id` and each task carries every
958	  processing-task field plus `runs`; `runs` is sorted by `attempt` and each
959	  run carries its run fields plus `proof`. `proof` re-runs the same checks as
960	  the per-run verify endpoint over that run's audit chain and is
961	  `{"valid", "checked_count", "last_evidence_hash"}`; `last_evidence_hash` is
962	  the stored evidence hash of the chain's final record and is `null` only for
963	  an empty chain — it is still returned when `valid` is `false`, and the run
964	  details are retained. Summary counters always agree with the returned
965	  details and the report is deterministic across restarts.
966	
967	### Processing run audit records (append-only proof chain)
968	
969	Every run carries an independent, tamper-evident chain of audit records.
970	Records are append-only (the database rejects updates and deletes, and there
971	are no per-record HTTP routes), numbered from `1` per run and linked through
972	SHA-256 evidence hashes. They persist across restarts.
973	
974	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/processing-tasks/{task_id}/runs/{run_id}/audit-records` —
975	  append a record. Body contains exactly `event`, `input_summary` and
976	  `result_summary`, each a string that is non-empty after trimming whitespace.
977	  Returns `201` with the submitted fields plus `id`, `sequence` (continuous
978	  from `1` within the run), `run_status` (the run's status at write time:
979	  `running`/`succeeded`/`failed`), `previous_hash` (`null` for the first
980	  record, otherwise the previous record's `evidence_hash`), `evidence_hash`
981	  and `created_at`. Missing, extra, non-string or blank fields → `422` and
982	  nothing is written; unknown dataset/version/task/run → `404`; a run that
983	  does not belong to the path task (including one in another version) →
984	  `422`. Concurrent appends never reuse a sequence or break the chain.
985	- `GET .../runs/{run_id}/audit-records` — list the run's records in ascending
986	  `sequence` order. Same `404`/`422` path rules.
987	- `GET .../runs/{run_id}/audit-records/verify` — verify the chain. Returns the
988	  path identifiers together with `valid` and `checked_count`:
989	  `{"dataset", "version", "task_id", "run_id", "valid", "checked_count"}`.
990	  Verification recomputes every `evidence_hash`, checks that `sequence` values
991	  are continuous from `1` and that each `previous_hash` equals the preceding
992	  record's `evidence_hash` (the first must be `null`). An intact chain returns
993	  `"valid": true` (also for an empty chain).
994	
995	`evidence_hash` is the hexadecimal SHA-256 of a canonical JSON document built
996	from every stored field except `id`, `created_at` and `evidence_hash` itself
997	(`event`, `input_summary`, `result_summary`, `sequence`, `run_status`,
998	`previous_hash`): keys are sorted by Unicode code point, no insignificant
999	whitespace is emitted and the text is UTF-8 encoded.
1000
